items.title: Uniform rigid-particle pressure correction and perturbative annealed mixed-norm Stokes regularity
items.difficulty_reason: H2: ordinary Meyers, Gehring and Shen estimates are allowed inputs. The remaining construction repairs a divergence solver to be constant inside every rigid inclusion, including particles meeting the reference ball boundary, while retaining constants uniform in the ball and particle count. This permits uniform pressure absorption in the rigid-compatible Caccioppoli estimate and the subsequent space/probability mixed-norm transfer from fluid to particle interiors. The pressure lemma, deterministic estimate and annealed theorem form one core.

rows.title: Logarithmically renormalized immersed-boundary approximation of steady Stokes flow around finitely many separated slender rigid filaments
rows.difficulty_reason: The centerline Stokeslet formula and minimum-dissipation principle do not give uniform errors as filament capacity degenerates. The authors prove the boundary and near-centerline asymptotics, construct divergence-free extensions with constants uniform in filament thickness, and build a capacitary test field for the local Sobolev error. These estimates produce the stated different logarithmic rates rather than a direct formal rescaling of a fixed-domain bound.

rows.title: Hölder spectral regularity and uniform twisted-integral bounds for random S-adic suspensions on eligible Oseledets roof subspaces
rows.difficulty_reason: H2: beyond the already counted corrected exceptional-dimension construction, the author must turn vector lattice escape into a uniform spectral estimate across all frequencies in a fixed band and all weakly Lipschitz observables. This uses population-vector lattice comparisons, a product estimate with its exact cylinder-level threshold, and the logarithmic choice of approximation level that balances the nonconstant roof/cylinder errors with the desired power. The argument then transports the estimate through nonuniform first-return inducing and telescoping while preserving the normalized roof slice, eligible Oseledets subspace and weak-Lipschitz norm. All these new source-local estimates and transport steps are supplied together; the old nonroutine dimension core remains explicit input and is not counted again.

rows.title: For regular finitely summable spectral triples with invertible weight, holomorphic dimension-spectrum control, bounded pole multiplicity and negative-integer spectrum stability, the finite-part zeta trace vanishes on commutators whose summed orders avoid the negative dimension spectrum
rows.difficulty_reason: Ordinary trace cyclicity does not survive finite-part regularization: commutators create higher residue defects. The author first constructs meromorphic traces of holomorphic abstract operator families, tracks their order and logarithmic derivatives, and expresses every defect through a finite higher-residue expansion. Dimension-spectrum translation stability then forces all relevant residue terms to vanish at admissible orders, producing the canonical commutator property without assuming a classical manifold calculus.

rows.title: Modulated-energy relaxation, Faxen approximation and the pre-collision zero-thickness limit of finitely many slender rigid filaments

actual_statement_excerpts.statement:
The system \eqref{N-S} is a second-order system whereas the limit equations \eqref{fav} are {first-order equations}. Therefore one initial data has to be dropped for the limit system \eqref{fav}. Unless
the initial data for the system \eqref{N-S} satisfies the compatibility conditions $(\textrm{v}_i (0),\omega_i (0)) = (\hat{\textrm{v}}_i(0),{\hat \omega}_i (0))$, for all $1 \leq i \leq N$, with $(\hat{\textrm{v}}_i(t),{\hat \omega}_i (t))$ given by \eqref{fav},
the velocities dynamics exhibit {an} initial layer, which prevents
uniform convergence of the filament velocities down to the initial time.
Indeed a byproduct of our analysis is that
we are able to describe the nature of the initial stage: it is an exponential relaxation within a time interval of order
$O(\eps^2 \log \eps)${. During that} time,
a transition of the amplitudes of the filament velocities occurs which is of order $O(1)$. After this initial stage, the dynamics of the filaments is adapted to the first-order dynamics of the limit system and the convergence occurs at least with a rate $O(\left|\log \eps \right|^{-\sfrac12})$.
More precisely, {for any $T < \hat T$ there is $\eps_0 > 0$ and $C>0$ as in Theorem~\ref{main}} such that for any $\eps $ in $(0,\eps_0)$, for any $1 \leq i \leq N$, and for any $t$ in $[0,T]$,%
\begin{multline}
\left| ({\textrm{v}}_i,\omega_{i})(t) - ({\hat {\textrm{v}}}_i, \hat \omega_i) (t) \right|\\
\leq \left| (\textrm{v}_i,\omega_i) (0)-
(\hat{\textrm{v}}_i,{\hat \omega}_i) (0) \right| \, e^{- \sfrac{C t}{\eps^2 \left|\log \eps\right|}} + C \left|\log \eps\right|^{-\sfrac12} e^{Ct}. \label{allezesti}
\end{multline}
